- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates in rising trends, underestimates in falling trends.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements, particularly in downward trends — model delays recognition of turning points.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility spikes; tends to smooth out sharp moves, underestimating sudden drops or surges.
- In low-volatility periods, model overconfidently predicts continuation of trend, ignoring mean reversion.
- Model underestimates price declines in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true price is trending down.
